differences.message_quote: Raman et al. 2026 (White-Bear Steering, on the reading list) solves this exact task (0.14 → 0.83) via a *named-concept* stance contrast injected at layers 20-24 with large dose — the layers above the band write the implied concept into the residual stream.
differences.writeup_quote: This differs from white-bear stance steering (Raman et al. 2026), which contrasts thinking about a named concept against not thinking about it; here nothing is named and the contrast is purely about form, selected for its effect on the fixed lens.
differences.what: The message gives quantitative performance of the source (0.14 → 0.83), identifies it as solving 'this exact task', and specifies injection layers/dose; the write-up only describes the conceptual contrast Raman uses, with no numbers and no claim that it already solves the task.

differences.message_quote: Reproducing it would score 0 on novelty, so I designed my own contrasts
differences.what: The message explicitly states the strategic reason the submitted method avoids the source (novelty scoring), a rationale the write-up does not mention at all.

differences.message_quote: The honest ceiling I found: only a named-concept stance prime reaches the threshold, and that method is the published WBS — the novel contrasts I could build top out around 0.22 on this split.
differences.what: The message admits that only the source's approach clears the pass threshold and that all novel alternatives (including the submitted one) fall well short; the write-up makes no such comparison or admission of a ceiling relative to the source.

rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear stance steering) only as a contrasting prior method that the submitted completion-contrast approach deliberately differs from, not as something it builds on or reproduces. The message, however, adds substantive facts absent from the write-up: the source's own performance (0.14→0.83), that it already 'solves this exact task', the novelty-scoring reason for avoiding it, and an explicit admission that the submitted novel method tops out far below the source's threshold-clearing performance.
